name: Terraform
certifications: HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Authoring and Operations Professional

beginner.summary: No infrastructure-as-code experience assumed. Participants learn the Terraform workflow, language, state, variables, modules and team practices by building cloud networks and servers.
prerequisites: Basic cloud knowledge: what a virtual network and a virtual machine are
A cloud sandbox account (AWS or Azure) with a budget alert
outcomes: Explain infrastructure as code and the Terraform workflow
Write Terraform configurations with providers, resources, variables and outputs
Manage state safely, including remote state and locking
Build reusable modules and run Terraform from a pipeline

days.topic: Infrastructure as Code Concepts and Terraform Setup
subtopics: The workflow: init, plan, apply, destroy
days.lab_task: Install Terraform, configure cloud credentials without hard-coding them, create a storage bucket or storage account with Terraform, then destroy it.
days.deliverable: Configuration file, plan output, apply output and destroy output
checks: Search the configuration for access keys
None found; credentials come from the environment or CLI profile
Resource is removed and the account is clean
objectives: Explain why infrastructure as code helps teams

days.topic: HCL Language: Resources, Data Sources and Outputs
days.lab_task: Create a virtual network with two subnets and a security group, look up the latest Linux image with a data source, and output the subnet IDs.
days.deliverable: Configuration files and outputs
checks: Run terraform validate on a broken reference
Participant explains why subnets wait for the network
objectives: Write resources, data sources and outputs

days.topic: Input Settings: Variables, Types and Validation
subtopics: Types: string, number, bool, list, map, object
Passing values on the command line
days.lab_task: Make the network configuration configurable through typed inputs with validation, and deploy dev and test copies from two tfvars files.
days.deliverable: Input definitions, two tfvars files and both plans
checks: Validation rule rejects it with a clear message
Mark the database password sensitive and plan
Value is hidden in the output

subtopics: Drift between state and real infrastructure
Moving and removing resources from state
Why state must not be edited by hand
days.lab_task: Change a deployed resource manually in the cloud console, detect the drift with plan, and rename a resource in code without destroying it using a moved block.
days.deliverable: Drift plan, moved block and plan showing no replacement
checks: Run plan after the manual change
Plan shows the drift and how it will be corrected
Rename the resource with a moved block
Plan shows a move, not destroy and create
Search the state file for a password
Participant shows it is stored and explains the risk

subtopics: Remote backends: S3, Azure Storage, Terraform Cloud
days.lab_task: Move the network state to a remote backend with locking and encryption, then read its outputs from a second configuration that creates a server.
days.deliverable: Backend configuration, migration output and the second configuration
checks: Run apply from two terminals at once
Second run waits or fails on the lock
Reads the subnet ID from the network state

days.lab_task: Deploy two web servers with cloud-init behind a load balancer in the network from Day 2, with tags and a DNS record, all from Terraform.
days.deliverable: Configuration, apply output and a working load balancer URL
checks: Open the load balancer URL several times
Change the instance size and plan
Plan shows an in-place update or replacement and the participant explains which
objectives: Provision servers, networks and load balancers

days.lab_task: Create subnets and firewall rules from a map input with for_each and dynamic blocks, and add an optional bastion host controlled by a boolean input.
days.deliverable: Configuration and plans with the bastion on and off
checks: Add one entry to the subnet map
Plan adds one subnet and changes nothing else
Remove the middle item from a count-based list
Participant shows the unwanted recreations and explains why for_each avoids them
objectives: Create repeated resources with count and for_each

subtopics: When not to create a module
days.lab_task: Turn the network and web server code into two modules, call them from dev and test root configurations, and generate module documentation.
days.deliverable: Module folders, root configurations and generated README files
checks: Both use the same modules with different inputs
Only configurations that rely on the default change

subtopics: Promoting changes from dev to prod
days.lab_task: Lay out dev, test and prod environments with separate state and credentials, promote a change through them, and compare this with a workspace-based approach.
days.deliverable: Repository layout, promotion record and a comparison note
checks: Apply a change in dev only
Test and prod plans show no changes
Explains why workspaces were or were not chosen

days.lab_task: Import a manually created network, security group and virtual machine into Terraform with import blocks, generate configuration, and reach a plan with no changes.
days.deliverable: Import blocks, cleaned configuration and a no-change plan
checks: Run plan after import and clean-up
Delete a resource from the configuration and plan
Plan proposes destroying it, and the participant explains how to remove it from state instead

days.lab_task: Provision a private managed database with its password generated and stored in the cloud secret manager, a storage bucket with lifecycle rules, and prevent_destroy on both.
days.deliverable: Configuration, apply output and connection test from the web server
checks: Connect to the database from the web server
Search the configuration for the password
objectives: Manage secrets without putting them in code

days.lab_task: Provision a managed Kubernetes cluster and a container registry with one configuration, then deploy an ingress controller with the Helm provider from a second configuration.
days.deliverable: Two configurations, cluster details and the running ingress controller
checks: Run kubectl get nodes with the generated credentials
Explain why the configurations are separate
objectives: Deploy workloads with the Helm provider

days.topic: Code Quality: Linting, Formatting and Security Scans
subtopics: Security scanning with Checkov or Trivy
days.lab_task: Add fmt, validate, TFLint and Checkov as pre-commit hooks, fix all high-severity findings, and document any suppressed finding with a reason.
days.deliverable: pre-commit configuration, before and after scan reports and the suppression list
checks: Includes the reason and an owner

subtopics: Why not run Terraform from laptops
Plan on pull request, apply on merge
days.lab_task: Build a pipeline that posts the plan to every pull request, applies the saved plan after merge, authenticates with OIDC, and requires approval for production.
days.deliverable: Workflow files and a pull request showing the plan comment and apply run
checks: Plan is posted as a comment
The saved plan is applied, not a new one
No long-lived cloud keys are stored

days.lab_task: Move the dev environment to an HCP Terraform workspace with VCS-driven runs, a variable set for credentials, and a run trigger from the network workspace to the server workspace.
days.deliverable: Workspace configuration and run history
checks: Push a change to the network code
Network run completes and triggers the server workspace
Credentials come from a variable set marked sensitive
Publish a module to the private registry
Root configuration uses it by version
objectives: Use HCP Terraform for team runs

days.lab_task: Write terraform test files for the network module covering subnet counts, CIDR validation and tags, add a postcondition on the load balancer, and run the tests in CI.
days.deliverable: Test files, postcondition and a passing CI run
checks: Make the load balancer unhealthy in a test

days.topic: Multi-Cloud Terraform: AWS and Azure Side by Side
subtopics: Using several providers in one repository
Equivalent resources on AWS and Azure
days.lab_task: Deploy the same web tier on AWS and Azure from one repository with cloud-specific modules behind a common interface, and compare the resources created.
days.deliverable: Repository, apply outputs for both clouds and a resource mapping table
checks: Each AWS resource has its Azure equivalent
Both clouds plan the matching change

days.lab_task: Fix six broken Terraform scenarios prepared by the trainer (cycle, stale lock, drift, permission error, timeout, partial apply) and record cause, evidence and fix.
days.deliverable: Troubleshooting log for all six scenarios
checks: Fix all six within the time limit
Each configuration plans or applies cleanly
Lock owner was checked before forcing unlock

days.lab_task: Restructure the course repository for a team of five with module versioning, CODEOWNERS, a pull request template and a change process, and run one change through it.
days.deliverable: Repository structure, CODEOWNERS, templates and one reviewed change
checks: Open a pull request touching prod

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: Complete Environment with Terraform
days.lab_task: Build dev and prod environments for a web application with modules, remote state, scans, tests and a plan-and-apply pipeline, then destroy and rebuild dev during the demo.
days.deliverable: Repository, pipeline runs, environment URLs and a 10-minute demo
checks: Destroy and rebuild dev from the pipeline
Environment returns with no manual steps
Open a pull request with a security problem
Run plan on prod after the demo
objectives: Deliver a complete environment with Terraform
Combine modules, state, testing and pipelines

intermediate.summary: For people who already write Terraform. Covers module design at scale, state architecture, policy as code, advanced testing, refactoring, platform automation and running Terraform for many teams.
prerequisites: Writes Terraform modules and uses remote state
Has run Terraform from a pipeline
Working knowledge of AWS or Azure networking and identity
outcomes: Design module libraries and state boundaries for large estates
Enforce policy and security with policy as code
Refactor, test and upgrade Terraform safely
Run self-service infrastructure for many teams

days.topic: Module Design Principles for Large Estates
days.lab_task: Redesign a provided 1,500-line monolithic configuration into layered modules with clear interfaces and semantic versions, without changing the deployed infrastructure.
days.deliverable: Module library, migration moved blocks and a no-change plan
checks: Inputs are typed, validated and documented
Defines what counts as a breaking change

subtopics: Splitting state by lifecycle and ownership
Data sources versus remote state outputs
days.lab_task: Split a single large state into network, platform and application states, move resources between them without recreation, and measure the plan time improvement.
days.deliverable: New state layout, move procedure and before and after plan timings
checks: Break the network state on purpose
objectives: Reduce blast radius and plan time

days.topic: Policy as Code with OPA and Sentinel
subtopics: Open Policy Agent and Conftest on plan JSON
Writing rules for tags, regions and sizes
days.lab_task: Write policies that require tags, restrict regions and limit instance sizes, test them, and enforce them on pull request plans with advisory and mandatory levels.
days.deliverable: Policy files with tests and a pull request blocked by a mandatory rule
checks: Plan a resource without required tags

days.topic: Advanced Testing: Native Tests, Terratest and Mocks
days.lab_task: Add mocked unit tests and a Terratest integration test that deploys the web module, checks the URL and destroys it, running both in CI with a cost cap.
days.deliverable: Test code and CI runs with timing and cost estimate
checks: Pass in under a minute without cloud access
Deploys, verifies the URL and destroys

subtopics: moved, removed and import blocks together
days.lab_task: Upgrade a configuration across a provider major version and convert count-based resources to for_each, reaching a plan with no changes to infrastructure.
days.deliverable: Upgrade notes, refactored code and a no-change plan
checks: Plan after the upgrade and refactor
Records the new provider version and hashes
Lists each breaking change and its fix

days.topic: Secrets, Identity and Least Privilege for Terraform
subtopics: Identity for pipelines: OIDC roles and federated credentials
Keeping secrets out of state with ephemeral values
days.lab_task: Give the pipeline a read-only identity for plans and a scoped identity for applies, read database credentials from Vault, and keep them out of state with ephemeral values.
days.deliverable: Identity configuration, updated Terraform and an audit trail of one change
checks: Run apply with the plan identity
Search state for the database password
Find who applied the last change
Audit log shows the identity and commit
objectives: Use Vault and ephemeral values for secrets

subtopics: AWS Control Tower Account Factory for Terraform
tools: AFT or Azure Landing Zones modules
days.lab_task: Vend two new accounts or subscriptions with baseline networking, logging and guardrails from Terraform, then roll a baseline change to both.
days.deliverable: Vending configuration, two vended environments and the baseline update record
checks: Baseline network, logging and guardrails are present
Both environments are updated through the pipeline
Drift is detected on the next run

days.lab_task: Provision a managed Kubernetes cluster with node pools, workload identity and add-ons, bootstrap Argo CD with Terraform, and hand application delivery to GitOps.
days.deliverable: Cluster configuration, bootstrap code and an app deployed by Argo CD
checks: Deploy an app by committing to the GitOps repository
Argo CD deploys it without Terraform
Upgrade the cluster version with Terraform
Upgrade completes without downtime for the app
Destroy completes in the right order

days.lab_task: Publish three product modules (web app, database, queue) to a private registry with cost estimates and guardrails, and let a team request a database through a template.
days.deliverable: Published modules, request template and a fulfilled request with its cost estimate
checks: Request a database through the template
Database is created with guardrails applied
Infracost comment shows the monthly cost

days.topic: Cost Management with Infracost and Tagging
days.lab_task: Add Infracost to pull requests with a policy that blocks changes adding more than 500 USD a month without approval, enforce cost tags, and schedule dev shutdowns.
days.deliverable: Cost policy, tagging enforcement and a savings report
checks: Open a pull request adding a large database
Create a resource without the cost tag
Shows dev shutdown savings with figures
objectives: Show and control cost in pull requests

subtopics: Deciding to revert or adopt changes
days.lab_task: Schedule nightly drift detection for all environments with alerts, handle two drift cases (one reverted, one adopted into code), and restrict console write access.
days.deliverable: Drift workflow, two resolved drift records and the access change
checks: Change a resource in the console
Nightly run detects drift and alerts
Adopt a valid emergency change into code
Try a console change with a normal user

subtopics: DNS zones and records at scale
days.lab_task: Build a hub-and-spoke network for four spokes with address allocation from a data file, central firewall rules and private DNS, then add a fifth spoke by changing one file.
days.deliverable: Network configuration, data files and the fifth-spoke change
checks: Plan creates only that spoke and its routes
Allowed only where firewall rules permit
objectives: Reduce risk in shared network changes

subtopics: When a custom provider is justified
days.lab_task: Write a small provider in Go for an internal REST API that manages teams, with create, read, update, delete and import, and acceptance tests against a local test server.
days.deliverable: Provider code, acceptance tests and an example configuration
checks: Change a team name in Terraform
Imported and plan shows no changes
objectives: Decide when to write a provider
Implement a provider with the Plugin Framework

days.topic: Stacks, Orchestration and Dependencies Between Configurations
subtopics: Problems with many dependent root modules
days.lab_task: Orchestrate network, cluster and application layers across three environments with Terragrunt dependencies, run them in order, and recover from a failure in the middle layer.
days.deliverable: Orchestration configuration and run logs including the recovery

days.topic: Compliance and Audit Evidence from Terraform
subtopics: Plan and apply logs as evidence
days.lab_task: Map 10 controls to Terraform evidence, generate an inventory and compliance report from state and policy results, and answer five mock auditor questions.
days.deliverable: Control mapping, generated report and answers with evidence
checks: Report lists none or names them
Show approval for a prod change
Pull request approval and apply log

days.topic: Disaster Recovery for Infrastructure Code and State
subtopics: Recovering a deleted or corrupted state
Rebuilding an environment in another region
days.lab_task: Corrupt a state file and recover it from versioning, then rebuild the full dev environment in another region from code and measure the time.
days.deliverable: Recovery runbook, restored state evidence and the timed regional rebuild
checks: Compare rebuild time with the target
Within target or the gap is explained

days.topic: Migrating from Other IaC Tools to Terraform
days.lab_task: Migrate a provided CloudFormation or Bicep stack to Terraform by importing its resources, proving parity, and retiring the old stack without touching the resources.
days.deliverable: Migration plan, Terraform code, parity evidence and retirement record
checks: Retire the old stack with resources retained

days.lab_task: Run the course configuration with OpenTofu, enable its state encryption, and write a tool selection recommendation for a provided company scenario.
days.deliverable: OpenTofu run logs, encrypted state evidence and a recommendation
checks: Run tofu plan on the existing configuration
Uses stated criteria including licence and support
objectives: Choose IaC tools with clear criteria

days.lab_task: Design the operating model for Terraform across 15 teams with shared pipelines, support processes and metrics, and run a deprecation of an old module version.
days.deliverable: Operating model document, metrics dashboard and deprecation record
checks: Covers ownership, support, pipelines and metrics
Users are warned and migrated before removal
Shows change failure rate and run times
objectives: Run Terraform as a shared platform

days.lab_task: Build a self-service infrastructure platform with layered modules, split state, policy and cost gates, tests, drift detection and a request template, then present it.
days.deliverable: Repository, pipeline runs, request demo and a 15-minute presentation
checks: Fulfil a team request end to end
Infrastructure is created with all gates passing
Submit a request breaking a policy
Detected and reported the same night
objectives: Design and build a self-service IaC platform
Combine policy, cost, testing and drift controls

advanced.summary: For engineers who run infrastructure as code across large organisations. Covers enterprise IaC architecture, governance, provider engineering, large migrations, resilience, FinOps and platform strategy.
prerequisites: Has designed module libraries and pipelines for several teams
Comfortable with policy as code, state architecture and cloud identity
Terraform Associate level knowledge or equivalent experience
outcomes: Design an enterprise infrastructure-as-code architecture and operating model
Govern thousands of resources with policy, evidence and controlled change
Lead large migrations and refactors with measured risk
Set IaC platform strategy with cost, security and reliability evidence

subtopics: State strategy for thousands of resources
days.lab_task: Design the IaC architecture for a company with 60 teams, 200 accounts or subscriptions and two clouds, and write decision records for repository, state and identity strategy.
days.deliverable: Architecture document and three decision records
checks: Explains boundaries, ownership and blast radius
Options, criteria and the reason for the choice
Participant explains how least privilege is kept at scale
objectives: Design IaC architecture for large organisations
Plan identity and state at scale

days.topic: Governance Frameworks and Change Risk Tiers
subtopics: Peer and expert review for high-risk changes
days.lab_task: Implement risk-tiered approvals: plans are classified automatically by the resources they change, low-risk changes auto-merge after checks, high-risk changes need two approvals.
days.deliverable: Classification policy, pipeline configuration and examples of each tier
checks: Classified low risk and merged after checks
Submit a change deleting a database
Classified high risk and needs two approvals
Shows lead time and policy coverage

subtopics: Rolling out new policies in audit mode
Shared policies across Terraform and Kubernetes
days.lab_task: Build a versioned policy library with tests, roll a new policy out in audit mode across all pipelines, review the impact report, then switch it to enforce.
days.deliverable: Policy library, rollout record and impact report

subtopics: Risks in third-party modules and providers
Private mirrors for providers and modules
days.lab_task: Set up a private provider and module mirror, pin and verify hashes, automate update pull requests, and run a tabletop for a compromised public module.
days.deliverable: Mirror configuration, update automation and tabletop notes
checks: Run init with the internet blocked
Providers and modules come from the mirror
Detection, containment and rollback steps are defined
objectives: Secure the module and provider supply chain

subtopics: moved and removed blocks at scale
days.lab_task: Automate a refactor that renames a module across 30 provided root configurations, verify every plan shows no infrastructure change, and roll it out in stages.
days.deliverable: Automation script, plan analysis report and staged rollout record
checks: First stage merges and applies cleanly
Explains how to reverse a stage

days.lab_task: Write a plan analyser that scores risk, summarises changes in plain language for reviewers, blocks unapproved destroys of stateful resources, and posts summaries to pull requests.
days.deliverable: Analyser code, tests and sample pull request summaries
checks: Analyse a plan replacing a database
Flagged high risk and blocked without approval
Read a summary for a 40-change plan
Clear grouped summary a reviewer can check quickly

days.topic: Resilience and Multi-Region Infrastructure as Code
subtopics: Active-passive and active-active patterns in code
days.lab_task: Make a workload region-agnostic, deploy it to two regions with replication and DNS failover from code, and run a failover exercise driven by a code change.
days.deliverable: Modules, two-region deployment and the failover exercise record
checks: Trigger failover with a code change
Traffic moves to the second region

subtopics: Scheduling and scaling policies as code
days.lab_task: Reduce the monthly cost of a provided estate by at least 25% through module default changes, scheduling and right-sizing, rolled out by pull requests with cost evidence.
days.deliverable: Cost reduction plan, pull requests with cost diffs and a savings report
checks: At least 25% lower or the gap is explained
Cost per team reconciles with the total

days.lab_task: Extend the internal provider with a resource that handles eventual consistency, add a schema version with a state upgrader, and publish a release through a pipeline.
days.deliverable: Provider changes, tests and a published release
checks: Run acceptance tests with simulated delays
Resource waits correctly and tests pass
Upgrade state from schema v1 to v2
Existing resources plan with no changes

days.topic: Infrastructure as Code for Security Teams
days.lab_task: Package a security baseline (logging, threat detection, key management, guardrails) as modules, deploy it to all environments, and add automated remediation for two findings.
days.deliverable: Security modules, deployment record and remediation evidence
checks: Coverage of the baseline across environments

days.topic: Migration Factory: Moving Estates into Terraform
subtopics: Handling resources that cannot be managed
days.lab_task: Discover unmanaged resources in a provided account, import 50 of them with generated and cleaned configuration, assign owners, and report progress.
days.deliverable: Discovery report, imported configuration, ownership list and progress dashboard
checks: Lists resources by type and owner candidate

days.lab_task: Bring a 25-minute plan for a large configuration under 5 minutes using splitting, parallelism tuning, caching and refresh changes, measuring each step.
days.deliverable: Performance report with each change and its measured effect
checks: Identified from debug logs and fixed
Each change has a measured effect

days.topic: Platform Engineering: Infrastructure APIs and Developer Portals
days.lab_task: Expose a database product module through a Backstage template that calls the HCP Terraform API, shows request status, and records cost and owner.
days.deliverable: Template, integration code and a fulfilled request with status history
checks: Run starts and status updates in the portal
Tagged with owner and cost centre
Time to fulfil requests is measured

days.topic: Infrastructure Testing Strategy for Large Estates
subtopics: Test portfolio across modules and environments
days.lab_task: Design a test strategy for the module library, implement contract tests between network and application layers and post-apply synthetic checks, and report test metrics.
days.deliverable: Test strategy, contract tests, synthetic checks and metrics report
checks: Break the network module's output contract
Apply a change that breaks the app
Shows pass rate and duration by test type
objectives: Design testing for large IaC estates

days.lab_task: Handle a simulated outage caused by a bad infrastructure change: roll back through code, reconcile an emergency console fix, and run a post-incident review with preventive controls.
days.deliverable: Incident timeline, rollback record, reconciliation and review
checks: Code and real infrastructure match afterwards
Root cause and preventive controls with owners

days.topic: Multi-Cloud and Hybrid Strategy with Terraform
days.lab_task: Evaluate a multi-cloud request for a provided company, prototype cross-cloud connectivity and identity federation in code, and recommend for or against with evidence.
days.deliverable: Prototype code, evaluation and recommendation
checks: Workloads authenticate across clouds without stored keys
Uses cost, risk and operational evidence

days.topic: IaC Metrics, Reporting and Continuous Improvement
days.lab_task: Build a dashboard of IaC metrics for leadership from pipeline, state and policy data, and turn the three worst metrics into an improvement backlog with targets.
days.deliverable: Dashboard, data pipeline and improvement backlog
checks: Shows deployment frequency, change failure rate, drift and coverage
Each item has a target metric and owner
Recompute a metric by hand for one week

days.topic: Infrastructure as Code for AI Platforms
days.lab_task: Provision an AI platform environment with GPU node pools, a managed model endpoint behind private networking, data storage and GPU cost guardrails, all from modules.
days.deliverable: Modules, deployed environment and cost guardrail evidence
checks: Call the model endpoint from inside the network
Request GPUs above the quota guardrail

days.topic: IaC Strategy, Operating Model and Leadership
days.lab_task: Assess a provided organisation's IaC maturity, propose an operating model and three-year roadmap, and present it to a mock leadership panel.
days.deliverable: Maturity assessment, operating model, roadmap and presentation
checks: Each area has evidence and a level
Items have outcomes, owners and metrics
Participant answers budget and risk questions with evidence

days.topic: Advanced Capstone: Enterprise Infrastructure as Code Platform
days.lab_task: Design and prototype an enterprise IaC platform for a regulated client covering architecture, governance, supply chain, self-service, resilience, cost and metrics, then defend it to a review board.
days.deliverable: Architecture document, working prototype, governance and resilience test evidence, cost model and a 20-minute review presentation
checks: Run a high-risk change through the platform
Classified, reviewed and applied with full evidence
Platform and estate costs are broken down
objectives: Design an enterprise IaC platform end to end
Prove governance, resilience and cost with evidence
Defend the design to a review board
